thread:
Lina V: Quick heads-up \/ Aurora Analytics asked for a console view that ties per-model-version cost to error fingerprints and a trace heatmap for spikes. They want to trial in 2 weeks. Need scope call.
Omar S: Can they accept estimated token costs or do they need exact billing numbers?
Priya K: They said 'close enough for engineering triage' not for invoicing. So estimated per-model-version + per-route is OK.
Jules M: tech note: we already emit model, route, and token_estimate in telemetry. We don't have an error fingerprint join to models. We can add a lightweight fingerprint tag on errors (hash of error class + prompt-id) and surface it. Low lift.
Lina V: good. Also they asked for a trace heatmap aggregated by minute with click-to-trace. Is click-to-trace feasible within retention limits?
Omar S: yes for recent data. retention tradeoff: hosted traces 14d by default. Heatmap pre-agg for 30d is feasible if we store minute-level counts only. Raw trace link only for 14d unless enterprise add-on.
Priya K: propose scope partition: A) Surface: Model-version cost estimate + p50/p95 latency tiles + error fingerprint counts (30d aggregated), B) Trace heatmap minute-buckets with click-to-trace for 14d, C) Export API for model-cost CSV (7d synchronous, 30d async).
Jules M: agree. For heatmap clicking into traces we'll add a pointer to `trace_id` when within 14d, otherwise show "trace expired" with option to request rehydrate (enterprise only).
Lina V: launch gates? Aurora wants: 1) ability to find top 5 error fingerprints by model-version, 2) jump from heatmap to trace within 2 clicks for recent windows, 3) cost CSV for 7d runs under 20s.
Omar S: infra constraints: CSV for large windows must be async with pre-signed S3 link. Also minute-level heatmap for 30d adds ~2% storage cost estimate. Will put numbers in doc.
Priya K: sampling during spikes: we should auto-elevate sampling to 100% for affected routes for 3 minutes after error rate > 5% over baseline. That gives us trace density to create heatmap patterns.
Jules M: implement as dataplane rule: when error-rate-threshold hit -> emit `sampling_override` event and annotate future spans with `fingerprint_id`. API for ops to trigger manual override: `POST /v1/ops/observability/override` with body `route, duration_s`.
ops-bot: release note: feature-branch observability/aurora-heatmap scheduled for staging deploy 2026-04-01T03:00Z.
Lina V: retention negotiation: Aurora requests 60d aggregated metrics and 45d raw traces. We push back: 60d aggregates OK, 45d raw traces only on private/dedicated plus add-on.
Omar S: alternative: offer on-demand rehydrate of raw traces from cold storage for an extra fee. Cheaper than full 45d hot retention.
Priya K: agreed. Customer-facing messaging: "30d hot traces, 60d aggregates, on-demand rehydrate for older traces (enterprise)". Lina please confirm with Aurora if they can accept that.
Lina V: will confirm. Action items: Omar  estimate infra cost delta for 30d minute-aggregates + CSV async job. Jules  PR for error fingerprint tagging + sampling override by 2026-03-27. Priya  dashboard mocks and CSV example. Lina  customer alignment and note on retention offer.
Jules M: risk log: heatmap UX may be noisy with high cardinality models; plan to limit to top N models by traffic and allow model filter. Not blocking.
Omar S: timeline: slice1 (fingerprint tagging + sampling override + dashboard mock) = 2 sprints. slice2 (heatmap + CSV export async + retention ops) = next sprint.
Priya K: success criteria for pilot: Aurora can (a) list top 5 error fingerprints by model-version, (b) click heatmap -> trace within 2 clicks for recent 7d window, (c) produce 7d cost CSV <20s.
Lina V: ok will get back to Aurora and lock pilot onboarding date. Thanks folks :rocket:
